where: /root/loop.sh on blaze-vm: a lane cannot compile before it pushes
what: The queue builds origin/int-1112 only, so the first compile of a change is after it is pushed to the branch every lane builds from. To keep the branch compiling this lane made a clone at /root/wt/sealed-1112/src with its own target directory, sent its working diff there (git diff piped to git apply) and ran cargo check and cargo test there, outside the queue: about 60 to 90 s a check on 128 cores, and it loads the machine other lanes time on.
cost: a second target directory (dev profile) and unqueued CPU; once, a git stash in that private clone to run a test on its base, which the rule forbids for shared worktrees
cause: loop.sh takes a branch, not a diff
workaround: the clone and /tmp/sealed-tools/check.sh on the Mac
fix: loop.sh takes an optional diff on stdin, applies it to a detached checkout, runs cargo check or the named tests in the shared warm target, and resets
whys: the queue was written for one writer of the branch
lanes write in one checkout but verify only after pushing
a push is the only way to hand the VM a tree
class: shared branch whose first compile is after the push
prevention: a check step in the queue that takes a diff, so no lane pushes what it has not compiled
